title: WPSS/642/2016 of Manoj Kumar Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.642/16
Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma, J.
 Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
 Mr. BPS Mer, Brief Holder, for the State.
 Process for filling up the posts of Primary
Teacher (Urdu) commenced on the basis of
advertisement dated 17.2.2016. Last date for receipt of
applications was 5.3.2016. Petitioner also participated
in the selection process. The candidature of the
petitioner was rejected primarily on two grounds; firstly
on the ground that the petitioner did not supply the 'No
Objection Certificate' from his previous employer and
the second being that he did not supply the
registration/renewal certificate from the respective
employment exchange.
 Attention of the Court has been drawn to
paragraph no.14 of the application form. According to
this document, there was no such requirement to supply
a 'No Objection Certificate' from the previous
employer. However, the petitioner has supplied the
same on 10.3.2016.
 Now, as far as the registration/ renewal of the
registration with the respective employment exchange is
concerned, petitioner was already serving as Gram
Panchayat Vikas Adhikari.
 Attention of the Court has been drawn to the
Government Order dated 8.8.2011, whereby the
employees, already serving in the State Government as
well as Central Government, are exempted from
registration/renewal in the respective employment
exchange. Moreover, their Lordships of Hon. Apex
Court in (2010) 11 Supreme Court Cases 674 in the case
of 'Union of India and others Vs. Pritilata Nanda' have
held that even though the employer is required to notify
the vacancies to the employment exchanges, it is not
obliged to recruit only those who are sponsored by the
employment exchanges. Their Lordships have held as
under: -
"16. In our opinion, there is no merit in the arguments of
the learned Additional Solicitor General. In the first place,
we consider it necessary to observe that the condition
embodied in the advertisement that the candidate should
get his/her name sponsored by any special employment

exchange or any ordinary employment exchange cannot be
equated with a mandatory provision incorporated in a
statute, the violation of which may visit the person
concerned with penal consequence.
17. The requirement of notifying the vacancies to the
employment exchange is embodied in the Employment
Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act,
1959 (for short "the 1959 Act"), but there is nothing in the
Act which obligates the employer to appoint only those who
are sponsored by the employment exchange.
18. A reading of the plain language of Section 4 makes it
clear that even though the employer is required to notify the
vacancies to the employment exchanges, it is not obliged to
recruit only those who are sponsored by the employment
exchanges.
20. The issue deserves to be considered from another
angle. It was neither the pleaded case of the appellants
before the Tribunal and the High Court nor was any evidence
produced by them to prove that the
Notification/Advertisement dated 31-1-1987 was sent to all
the employment exchanges including the special
employment exchanges in the State of Orissa. Before this
Court also, no document has been produced to show that the
advertisement was circulated to the employment exchanges
in the State. In this backdrop, it is not possible to approve the
stance of the appellants that the respondent was not
appointed because she did not get her candidature sponsored
by an employment exchange."
 It is also submitted at bar that the similarly
situate employees, who have not supplied the renewal/
registration certificate from the respective employment
exchange, have also been considered for appointment.
This averment has not specifically been denied by the
respondents in their reply. The action of the respondents
declaring the petitioner ineligible was arbitrary and
unreasonable.
 Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Respondents are directed to consider the candidature of
the petitioner for appointment on the post of Primary
Teacher (Urdu) within eight weeks from today.
 All pending applications stand disposed of
accordingly.
